positions.position: The inline negated compound expression `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` is harder to read than extracting a helper like `isStatementLayer(node)` or splitting into a positive condition. A small named helper would communicate intent (`@layer foo;` is fine, `@layer foo {}` is not).

The change is a one-line fix in a hot conditional; introducing a helper expands the diff and risks unrelated churn. Inline is acceptable given the surrounding pattern already uses similar inline checks.
Checking `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is the conventional PostCSS way to distinguish statement at-rules from block at-rules, since container nodes always have a `nodes` array even if empty.

Some prefer `node.nodes == null` or an explicit `Array.isArray(node.nodes)` check to be robust against unusual ASTs or plugins that might set `nodes` to `null`. The current check would treat `nodes: null` as a block, which may or may not be intended.

issues.description: Test only covers empty `@layer foo {}`; no test for `@layer foo { .a {} }` with actual contents
issues.detail: The added test uses `@layer foo {}` (empty block). While this exercises the new condition because `node.nodes` is defined (as an empty array) when a block is present, a non-empty layer block would be a more representative case and guard against regressions if the detection mechanism changes. Consider adding a case with `@layer foo { .a { color: red; } }` followed by `@import` to lock in the broader intent.

issues.description: Inline negated compound predicate reduces readability
issues.detail: The expression `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` packs the semantic distinction (statement-form `@layer` vs block-form `@layer`) into a negated conjunction inside an already long boolean. Extracting a small helper like `isLayerStatement(node)` or commenting the rationale (`@layer name;` is allowed before `@import` per spec; `@layer name {}` is not) would aid future maintainers.

issues.description: No test for the still-allowed case (`@layer foo;` before `@import`)
issues.detail: The PR adds a rejection test for layer-with-block but does not add (or reference) an accept test confirming that `@layer foo;` (statement form) before `@import` still passes. If such a test exists elsewhere in the suite it is fine, but explicitly pairing the new negative test with the corresponding positive case prevents accidental over-tightening later.

issues.description: Changeset entry classifies a bug fix as `minor`
issues.detail: The changeset declares this change as `minor`, but semver-style conventions (and stylelint's own past practice) typically classify a bug fix that produces additional warnings as `patch` or `minor` depending on whether it's considered a breaking lint behavior change. Worth confirming with maintainer convention; if new violations now surface in user code, `minor` is defensible, otherwise `patch` may be more appropriate.

review.summary: The fix correctly closes a gap in `no-invalid-position-at-import-rule` by treating block-form `@layer name {}` like other block at-rules (which invalidate a following `@import`), while still permitting statement-form `@layer name;` per the CSS cascade spec. The implementation uses the standard PostCSS idiom (`typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'`) and the change is minimal and well-scoped. The main improvement opportunities are around readability (the negated compound predicate is dense) and test coverage (only an empty-block case is added; a non-empty block case and an explicit positive test for statement-form `@layer` would harden the fix). No correctness blockers identified.
